neighbours.label: a judgment that an action is futile or pointless (useless, little point, a lost cause, hopeless, no use), as against judgments that the action is worthwhile
fire: After the third breakdown, fixing the old car seemed useless to her.
With the river this high, it was hopeless to try to cross before dark.
Everyone agreed there was little point in repainting the shed now.
By the last lap the race was a lost cause for the home team.
Shouting at the referee was no use; he never changed a call.
Arguing with the landlord about the rent felt completely futile.
My grandmother said worrying about the weather is pointless.
She knew any attempt to save the wilted roses was useless.
quiet: After the third breakdown, she drove the old car to the garage.
With the river this high, the ferry waited until morning to cross.
Everyone agreed the shed should be repainted green this summer.
By the last lap the home team had moved into second place.
The referee blew his whistle and the players walked off.
The talks with the landlord about the rent went well.
My grandmother said the weather would clear by the weekend.
She watered the wilted roses and they recovered by evening.
